newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GBL no comment on Suez stake.
newsitem.headline: GBL no comment on Suez stake.

text.p: Belgian holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert (GBL) on Monday declined to comment on a weekend report in daily L'Echo which said GBL had boosted its stake in French Compagnie de Suez to five percent.

A GBL unit acquired a 2.9 percent stake in Suez from Elf Aquitaine on October 7 and was reported by French financial daily newspaper L'Agefi on October 23 to have taken another one percent from French insurer UAP.
L'Echo quoted sources saying that since then GBL had boosted its stake to five percent and that a Suez board membership for GBL head Albert Frere was now a matter of weeks away.
The Belgian newspaper said GBL would before then have to report to French regulator Societe des Bourses Francaises (SBF) that its Suez stake had hit the five percent threshold.
A Suez spokeswoman in Paris also declined to comment.
Earlier today Suez Chairman Gerard Mestrallet reiterated, in an interview with French financial daily La Tribune Desfosses, that he would welcome Frere on the board of Suez.
"If Albert Frere could raise (his stake in Suez) to about five percent, I would be happy," he was quoted as saying.
